title: Insurtech claims automation pilot - SOW & workshop notes
content:
Purpose
This document captures the scope, deliverables, workshop agenda, rough pricing sketch, and open questions for a 6–8 week Claims Automation pilot with a mid-size US property & casualty insurer. Goal is to validate an LLM-assisted claims triage + intake prototype that reduces adjuster touch time and surfaces high-confidence structured outputs for downstream systems.

Context & goals (customer asks)
- Replace manual free-text triage for new first-notice-of-loss (FNOL) reports — extract claim type, severity bucket, party roles, policy references, and timeline.
- Provide suggested routing and estimated handling priority to reduce time-to-first-assignment.
- Integrate with agent desktop via webhook + structured JSON output.
- Evaluate accuracy, latency, and economics of hosted Redwood API vs Dedicated within insurer VPC for sensitive PII.

High-level approach
1) Discovery workshop (week 0): 2-hour remote session with claims ops, data, and security to collect sample FNOLs, define priority fields, and agree SLOs.
2) Data prep & sampling (week 1): ingest small sample (2k anonymized FNOL text snippets), generate test set (300 samples) and holdout evaluation set (200).
3) Prototype development (weeks 2–4): build prompt-suite + schema-guided extraction using a Redwood-verified open model variant; set up endpoint + output validation layer; add fallback routing rules.
4) Workshop + demo (end of week 4): show results to stakeholders, collect qualitative feedback, and finalize plan for controlled pilot.
5) Pilot deployment (weeks 5–8): run ingest of 10k live FNOLs in shadow mode (no production routing) with cost/latency monitoring.
6) Evaluation & handoff (week 8): provide evaluation report, suggested roll-out plan, and cost/architecture recommendations (hosted vs dedicated vs private).

Deliverables
- Workshop artifacts: attendee list, agenda notes, prioritized field list, and SLO matrix.
- Data snapshot: anonymized 2k sample + labeled 300 test set.
- Prototype endpoint: documented API contract, example payloads, and simple validation webhooks.
- Pilot report: accuracy/precision/recall by field, latency percentiles, cost per inference estimate, failure modes.
- Rollout recommendation: recommended deployment mode, quantization/latency tradeoffs, and gating criteria for production.

Success criteria (tentative)
- Extraction F1 >= 0.88 for "claim type" and "date of loss"; >= 0.80 across critical priority fields.
- 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for inference in Dedicated config (single-request path).
- Cost per FNOL inference <= $0.012 in recommended config (with batching and caching).
- Business acceptance: claims ops confirm >30% reduction in time-to-assign in shadow/case review exercise.

Workshop agenda (Discovery, 2 hours)
- 0:00–0:10: Introductions & pilot goals (Redwood SE + insurer claims lead)
- 0:10–0:30: Current FNOL flow + pain points (claims ops)
- 0:30–0:55: Data walk-through: sample records, PII concerns, retention rules (data engineering + security)
- 0:55–1:20: Define target outputs & priority fields; map to downstream systems (policy DB, assignment rules)
- 1:20–1:40: Latency/cost/accuracy tradeoffs & deployment constraints (security & infra)
- 1:40–2:00: Success metrics, timeline, owners, and next steps

Integration & tech notes
- Preferred integration: webhook to claims-api with structured JSON, optional human-in-the-loop review interface for low-confidence outputs.
- Validation: implement schema validator and simple heuristic checks (dates in range, policy id format).
- Fallbacks: on low-confidence, route to manual triage queue; on inference error, fallback to rules-based extractor (regex for policy numbers).
- Data security: propose two tracks — (A) hosted Redwood API with customer-provided redaction + contractual DPA; (B) Redwood Dedicated deployed inside customer VPC (preferred for PII-heavy flows).

Rough pricing & effort estimate (draft, non-binding)
- Fixed effort (SOW professional services): 6 weeks engagement, 0.6 FTE Redwood SE + 0.4 FTE Solutions Eng infra (setup + runbook) + 0.2 FTE PM = $72k (time & materials blended rate).
- Pilot hosting costs (approx):
  - Hosted (Redwood API): estimated compute + tokens for 10k FNOLs (avg 120 tokens) = ~$1,200 (API usage) + $200 for logging/observability retention.
  - Dedicated (short-term reserved capacity): setup + 4-week reserved = ~$9k–12k depending on GPU class; amortized per-FNOL estimate: $0.008–0.015.
- Optional on-prem/private deployment add-on: $35k one-time package (installation, validation, KMS integration) — recommended only if regulator requires it.
- Training & handoff workshop (2 days) = $6k.
- Contingency & change buffer: 15% on professional services estimate.

Assumptions & constraints
- Customer will provide anonymized sample data within 5 business days of signed SOW; data must be in CSV/JSON text format.
- No heavy label budget included — labeling beyond 1,000 samples will be scoped separately.
- Redwood will use open model variants verified for performance; if customer requires closed/proprietary model licensing, costs will change.
- Network egress costs for Dedicated inside customer VPC are borne by customer.

Open questions / risks
- Data quality: samples may be low-quality OCR outputs; need to confirm text extraction upstream.
- PII/legal: customer may require complete on-prem deployment which would extend timeline by 3–4 weeks.
- SLA expectations: production SLAs not part of pilot — only observational metrics.
- Edge cases: NLP hallucinations on novel policy wording — need manual review budget.

Key contacts
- Redwood: Maya Patel (SE, owner) — maya@redwood.example.com; Jonas Kim (infra lead) — jonas@redwood.example.com
- Customer (placeholder): Claims Ops lead: TBD; Data engineering: TBD

Next steps (immediate)
- Send this draft SOW + agenda to customer for review and pick a discovery workshop date.
- Customer to confirm sample data export and data access timeline.
- Redwood legal to prepare a short 6-week MSA addendum for pilot work, and a DPA addendum for hosted track.

Notes-to-self / internal TODOs
- Prepare demo notebook with 10 curated FNOLs showing high/low confidence outputs.
- Create evaluation sheet template (per-field confusion matrix + sample false positives).
- Align with infra on Dedicated sizing options and estimated price bands by GPU class.
